feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: NPR's expanded coverage of U.S. and world politics, the latest news from Congress and the White House and elections.

entry.title: Trump withdraws Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, as his nominee to lead ICE
entry.summary: The White House says it is withdrawing its nomination of Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, to lead ICE, ensuring that an agency at the forefront of President Trump's domestic agenda will remain without a Senate-confirmed leader for at least a while longer.

entry.title: 'American Scoundrel' traces Roy Cohn's playbook from McCarthyism to Trump
entry.summary: In Kai Bird's biography of Cohn, he looks at how the lawyer taught Trump how to deny, delay, attack, sue and countersue, never admit defeat, side-step paying bills and avoid a paper trail.

entry.title: D.C. airspace is complicated. Experts say Trump's arch would add one more risk
entry.summary: The Trump administration wants to build its 250-foot arch near one of the country's busiest runways. The FAA will determine whether that poses a hazard. But independent experts already have concerns.

entry.title: Big questions - and key logistical details - loom ahead of China-U.S. summit
entry.summary: Despite the lingering questions, China remains optimistic about the summit.

entry.title: Growing number of GOP candidates are using anti-Muslim rhetoric on the campaign trail
entry.summary: Anti-Muslim rhetoric has become increasingly common on the campaign trail at a moment when many Republicans are eager to shift attention away from the economy.

entry.title: House passes Russia sanctions, sending bill named for Lindsey Graham to Trump's desk
entry.summary: The legislation was named for the late South Carolina Republican. It gives the president authority to impose tariffs on top importers of oil and natural gas from Russia, such as China and India.

entry.title: House holds billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress over Epstein investigation
entry.summary: Billionaire investor Leon Black refused to appear before the committee investigating convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein for a deposition. Now it's up to the Department of Justice whether to pursue criminal charges.

entry.title: Congress is under pressure to act on AI — here's what that could look like
entry.summary: Lawmakers are expressing broader willingness to regulate AI development, but the path forward may not be a quick one.

entry.title: DOJ charges Russian agents with plotting attacks, including in the U.S.
entry.summary: The indictment says the defendants belong to a network that "is one arm of the Russian Federation's apparatus used to carry out external attacks" worldwide.

entry.title: A tumultuous congressional primary season closes with record departures and defeats
entry.summary: Already, close to 100 lawmakers who started this Congress will not be around for the next one, according to an NPR analysis, driven by record-setting retirements and primary defeats.
